A1.justification: Both PDFs describe Pro-Pose and contain readable main text, equations, figures, tables, references, and appendices A–E. Content can be reliably matched across relocation and renumbering.

before.justification: v2 reports original DeepFashion/WPose experiments, training-data and donor-masking ablations, personalization results, and identity-overfitting analyses.

after.justification: v3 retains those experiments and adds original VTO user-study results, body-skin and body-shape measurements, and a UV-conditioning ablation.

M1.justification: The core donor-masking, hybrid-training, flow-matching, and personalization procedures remain unchanged. Section 5 adds optional inference fallbacks for unreliable SMPL-X estimates: dropping pose conditioning or substituting a similar subject's shape parameters. The expanded conditioning-architecture description otherwise documents implementation rather than establishing a model redesign.

E1.justification: The training sources, DeepFashion/WPose benchmarks, and supplementary in-the-wild and personalization coverage are retained. The new body measurements, UV ablation, and controlled VTO study evaluate existing data and tasks; they do not establish additional dataset or task coverage.

E2.justification: Table 1 adds Gemini 3 Pro Image on both benchmarks while retaining Gemini 2.5 Flash Image. Figures 12 and 15 replace their Gemini 2.5 comparison columns with Gemini 3. The BC-input and face-region quantitative comparisons retain their previous comparator sets.

E3.justification: v3 introduces a pose-matched VTO study using 500 images, six garments, and ten raters, totaling 30K votes. It also adds segmented body-skin evaluation, SMPL-X shape-parameter distance/similarity metrics, and a paired-only training control without UV conditioning. Existing benchmark splits and main training budgets remain unchanged.

E4.justification: New analyses test whole-body preservation beyond facial identity (Appendix D.6), the contribution of UV conditioning alone (D.8), lighting behavior and Gemini failures (D.3), and VTO benefits with pose controlled (D.9). These substantially extend the retained donor-masking, training-data, personalization, and identity-overfitting analyses.

E5.justification: No new model-run counts, seeds, confidence intervals, or significance tests are reported. Existing shaded plots and distribution summaries are retained. The new VTO study supplies sample counts and aggregate percentages without introducing uncertainty estimates.

E6.justification: v3 adds Gemini 3 scores, body-preservation and UV-ablation results, and VTO preferences/errors, including 71.98% preference for Pro-Pose preprocessing. Existing Table 1 rows remain unchanged. The donor-ablation Ours row is revised from PSNR 19.87/FID 6.04 to 19.95/5.99 (v2 Table 3; v3 Table 4), without explaining whether experiments were rerun.

T1.justification: Equations 1–11 and the UV-visibility, flow-matching, personalization, and rasterization formulations remain mathematically unchanged. The added standard body-shape evaluation metrics do not introduce new theoretical results or proofs.

C1.justification: The abstract, introduction, and conclusion retain the same central contributions: donor-based UV self-supervision, joint paired/unpaired training, BC standardization, personalization, and identity-preserving portraits supporting VTO. Naming Gemini 3 in the evaluation contribution adds supporting evidence without redefining these claims.

C2.justification: v3 explains lighting behavior through BC standardization, argues for partial UV extraction over FreeUV, and interprets the UV ablation as locating the principal gains in unpaired-data learning. It also discusses the body-shape fidelity cost of inference fallbacks and attributes the VTO study's slight person-error increase to SMPL-X limitations.

D1.justification: New disclosures specify OminiControl-style token conditioning, LoRA masking and adapter locations, SMPLify-X estimation, original-image textures versus BC targets, and approximately 51-second inference. A project-page link is added. These are localized reproducibility additions; the PDFs do not establish a new code or data release.

R1.justification: v3 adds citations to Gemini 3 Pro Image, OminiControl, and FreeUV. It attributes the conditioning architecture to OminiControl and contrasts its full-body partial textures with FreeUV's facial generative recovery. The broader related-work organization and research positioning remain intact.

P1.justification: Most existing prose and the main section sequence are retained. Changes comprise localized methodological explanations, additional appendix subsections, wording edits, and author-affiliation information rather than extensive rewriting or narrative restructuring.

P2.justification: v3 substantially expands the displayed evidence with VTO-study, body-preservation, and UV-ablation tables (Tables 3, 7, 8), plus lighting and matched-pose VTO figures (Figures 16, 19). Comparison columns in Figures 12 and 15 are replaced, missing-image markers are clarified, and several existing displays are relocated. The underlying visual style is retained.

improvement.justification: v3 addresses important validation gaps: the full-body identity claim gains direct skin/shape measurements, and the previously illustrative VTO benefit gains a pose-controlled human evaluation. The UV ablation clarifies the source of improvement, while implementation disclosures improve reproducibility. The VTO study also exposes a small person-error tradeoff. Together, these substantially strengthen support for the existing claims despite remaining reporting imperfections.
